title: After All That I Have Done
description: After All That I Have Done in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 185.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Af-ter all that I have done, Sa-viour, art thou pa-ci-fied? Whith-er shall my vile-ness run? Hide me, earth, the sin-ner hide! Let me sink in-to the dust, Full of ho-ly shame, a-dore! Je-sus Christ, the good, the just, Bids me go, and sin no more.

lines: After all that I have done,
Hide me, earth, the sinner hide!
Let me sink into the dust,
Jesus Christ, the good, the just,
Bids me go, and sin no more.
Jesus, Son of God and man!
Let me never grieve thee, Lord,
Till my all in all thou art,
Till thou bring thy nature in,
Save me, save me, Lord, from sin!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
